## Part 1 – Load Required Libraries

-   In this assignment, we use several R packages to perform text mining, sentiment analysis, data manipulation, and visualization.

    ```{r}
    #| label: Required Libraries

    # Load required libraries

    library(tidyverse)
    library(tidytext)
    library(janeaustenr)
    library(stringr)
    library(wordcloud)
    library(RColorBrewer)

    ```

-   Explanation of the packages:

    -   tidyverse: Data manipulation and visualization

    -   tidytext: Text mining and sentiment analysis

    -   janeaustenr: Provides Jane Austen's books

    -   stringr: Text processing and regular expressions

    -   wordcloud: Creates word cloud visualizations

    -   RColorBrewer: Provides color palettes

## Part 2 – Data Preparation: Loading the Dataset

-   Data Preparation

    -   In this section, we load Jane Austen's books using the `janeaustenr` package and explore the available dataset. We will identify the different books and examine the structure of the text data.

    ```{r}
    #| label: Load Dataset

    # Load Jane Austen's books
    austen_data <- austen_books()

    # Display the first six rows
    head(austen_data)


    ```

-   Explanation:

    -   austen_books() loads the collection of Jane Austen's novels.
    -   We store the dataset in an object called austen_data.
    -   head() displays the first six rows so we can inspect the data.

-   Explore the available books

    -   The unique() function identifies the distinct book titles in the dataset. This allows us to confirm that Emma is included.

```{r}
#| label: Explore the available books

# Display all available book titles
unique(austen_data$book)

```

-   Examine the dataset structure
    -   glimpse() shows the columns and data types.
    -   count(book) calculates how many text lines are available for each novel.

```{r}
#| label: Dataset Structure

# Examine the structure of the dataset
glimpse(austen_data)

# Count the number of lines for each book
austen_data %>%
  count(book)

```
